mainText:
Lead item. Wildfires near Bordeaux and across central Spain have forced about three hundred and twenty thousand people from their homes. Another heatwave is forecast.

New Zealand.

Mauao at Mount Maunganui remains active after the main landslide from January reactivated over the weekend. Tauranga City Council says monitoring alarms activated again on Monday. The council says the landscape continues to change. The affected area is within the Mount Maunganui Beachside Holiday Park. The Government Inquiry into the fatal Tauranga landslides is also taking public submissions until five p.m. on Tuesday the eleventh of August.

New Zealand's revised school curriculum is moving towards fewer, larger achievement standards. The Ministry of Education says the existing number of assessments has increased workload for students and teachers. Revised standards and supporting material for a number of subjects across N.C.E.A. Levels One, Two and Three were published on Tuesday. The ministry says most of this year's maintenance changes are minor and do not change the competencies being assessed.

World.

Wildfires around Bordeaux in France and across central Spain have forced about three hundred and twenty thousand people to evacuate. Reuters reports about two hundred and twenty thousand evacuees in France and nearly one hundred thousand in Spain. Fires are still active in Madrid, Toledo, Avila and Castellon. France and Spain are using a period of better weather to contain the fires before temperatures rise again. International firefighting help has arrived from several European countries and Turkey.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is in Washington for his first meeting with United States President Donald Trump since the United States and Israel began their war with Iran. The White House says the leaders are also due to discuss the Israel and Lebanon framework agreement and possible expansion of the Abraham Accords. Trump says talks with Tehran have become friendlier. Iran says Washington is struggling to find a way out of the conflict.

Technology.

No technology or artificial intelligence item cleared today's higher corroboration gate.

Sport.

Formula One. Lando Norris won the Hungarian Grand Prix from pole for McLaren. Max Verstappen finished second, fifteen point zero eight zero seconds behind. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was third. Charles Leclerc finished fourth and Lewis Hamilton fifth. Liam Lawson started eleventh and finished eighth, one lap down, scoring four points. Norris's win was McLaren's first of the season. Formula One now enters its summer break.

Commonwealth Games. Lewis Clareburt has won New Zealand's first gold medal of the Glasgow Games in the men's two hundred metres butterfly. It follows his earlier silver in the two hundred metres individual medley. Erika Fairweather added silver in the fifteen hundred metres freestyle, her third medal of the Games. The Silver Ferns beat Jamaica fifty-three to forty-eight, their first win over Jamaica in almost four years. High jumper Hamish Kerr has withdrawn from the Games, saying he was not ready to compete at the level he expected.

Tennis. The four Grand Slam tournaments are between events. The United States Open main draw begins on Sunday the thirtieth of August in New York. The official player field is due to be released on Thursday the twentieth of August.

Premier League. Off-season. The new English league season has not started.

Bundesliga. Off-season. The new German league season has not started.

Champions League. Qualifying is in progress during the European summer.

All Blacks. No test today.

Chiefs. Super Rugby is off-season.

Coming up.

The Commonwealth Games continue in Glasgow. Formula One is on its summer break after Hungary. United States Open qualifying and fan week begin in August, with main-draw singles starting Sunday the thirtieth. The Tauranga landslide inquiry is accepting public submissions until Tuesday the eleventh of August.

End of flash.
